title: 'We don't work for AI': Greens vow to regulate artificial intelligence
key_facts: New Zealand's Green Party says that, if elected, it will regulate AI so that its benefits are shared with New Zealanders and not just the technology companies that operate it.
Co-leader Chlöe Swarbrick said AI should work for people and the planet: "We don't work for AI."

A party policy document says it would not allow fully automated decisions for anything that could make a substantive difference to people's lives in any public service, and that humans managing the tools must be able to make decisions.
It also calls for greater protection of data and explicit consent standards for AI training data.
The Greens want mandatory environmental impact assessments for hyperscale AI data centres, and new facilities to fully cover their own energy use.
The party also wants stronger enforcement of tax law so companies cannot take profits offshore, and worker participation in decisions about workplace AI adoption.

"The Greens will regulate it responsibly, for the public good.
why_it_matters_hint: A New Zealand party is putting AI rules for public services, data, data centres and workplaces into its election platform.
